title: 'How I bootstrapped The StoryGraph to nearly 3M users' with Nadia Odunayo.
description:
Nadia Odunayo didn't just start The StoryGraph – (the #1 competitor to Goodreads, with nearly 3M registered users.) She did it fully bootstrapped, using her personal savings to fund her runway. 

In just a few short years, Nadia combined her passion for reading with her coding expertise to create a successful, profitable company – built from the ground up. 

In this video, hear how she did it – with plenty of stories, strategies, and lessons learned from bootstrapping + building lean. 

If you’ve got a side project (or even just an idea), and want to know how you can build it into something more – you’re in the right place. 

🔸 What to look forward to in this session 🔸

- How she came up with (and evaluated) her idea 
​- The importance of user interviews
​- Personal runway and funding your startup
​- Creating effective product-led growth + marketing
​- Pros and cons of bootstrapping
​- Growing a community around your project
​- Coding as a one-woman dev team and wearing multiple hats
- ​The role of good and bad luck
- Her lowest moment in building the company
- One of her highest moments in the company

+ more of what Nadia has learned from bootstrapping, building, and scaling. 

If you’re on your tech side hustle journey, don’t start from square one. 
We’re here to give you insight and knowledge from those who have been there, done it, and succeeded.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Featured speaker: 
Nadia Odunayo is a developer, speaker, avid reader, and founder of The StoryGraph, the number one competitor to Goodreads (with nearly 3M registered users). After graduating from college, she learned to code at Makers Academy in London, going on to work as a software engineer at Pivotal. Combining her development expertise and love of books, she built The StroyGraph. In her spare time, when not reading, you'll likely find her at a dance class.
